title: When is a linear optimal power flow safe to dispatch from, and which cheap AC repair makes it safe?
lede: research programme on linear OPF dispatch feasibility on the PGLib-OPF benchmark: the DC dispatch overloads branches on all 11 congested cases; a trust-region successive linearisation of the AC power flow repairs 7 of 11 at the AC optimum's cost, and on 12 held-out angle-limited (SAD) cases the same rules with linearised angle rows repair 7 of 11 (angle-blind: 3); voltages held at the AC optimum's schedule
summary: An open research programme (opened 2026-11-12, track 21) on whether the dispatch from a linear optimal power flow, the model markets clear energy with, is feasible once the AC physics is applied, and how many AC power flows a repair needs to make it so at the AC optimum's cost. Benchmark: PGLib-OPF v23.07 (typical, congested API and small-angle-difference SAD sets of 12 cases, 14 to 300 buses), solved with PYPOWER, whose AC optima match the library's published values within 0.005 %. So far (experiments in infra-dcopf): the plain DC dispatch overloads branches on all 11 API cases with an AC optimum; a trust-region successive linearisation (finite-difference loss factors and flow sensitivities, a QP, an elastic l1 fallback) repairs 7 of 11 at the optimum's cost, with rules set on those cases; on the 12 SAD cases, held out, the same rules plus linearised angle-difference rows repair 7 of the 11 with an AC optimum, while the angle-blind version repairs 3 and lands 6.5–17.6 % below the optimum's cost by breaking up to 16 angle limits. Limits: voltages are held at the AC optimum's schedule (an oracle), one AC solver, one load point per case, no baseline yet from LPAC or optimised linearisations. Target: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems.
